non_blocking_notes: Write-set deviation (accepted): src/rivretrieve/_internal/station_map.py is modified but is not listed in the plan's section-3 write-set. The change is confined to deleting _filter_stations, _normalize_string_filter and _validate_bbox — helpers that became unreachable once map_stations() was withdrawn — plus their now-unused Sequence and FatalContractError imports. This is the correct dead-code outcome for this deletion and is exactly the pre-PR repair the review brief describes; noting only that the plan write-set never named the file.

Known and deliberately excluded: the module docstring at src/rivretrieve/_internal/station_map.py:1 still reads 'station map = render(filter(StationCatalog, provider IDs x bounding box), ...)' although the bounding-box filter is gone. Flagged per instruction, not blocked.

README.md:17-26 still shows rr.stations(), rr.provider("ch_foen") and rr.map_stations(providers="ch_foen") in the quickstart. Those three calls now raise AttributeError against the shipped surface. The plan explicitly prohibits documentation work in this step, so this is correctly out of scope here, but it is the highest-value follow-up before any release: the front-page example of the package is broken. docs/design/provider-redesign*.md also still describe the withdrawn handle/global-table API; those read as historical design records and are lower priority.

The step drops the _ensure_default_providers_registered() call that public provider() used to make before lookup (_provider_lookup is now bare _registry.get, as the plan mandates). This is safe only because every caller reaches _fetch_provider_series through a _Selection produced by find/pick/from_frame, each of which registers defaults first, and _require_selection rejects anything else. Worth remembering if a future caller ever reaches _provider_lookup on a cold registry; the rewritten provider tests all now call rr.providers() explicitly for exactly this reason.

Test quality is good on the rewrites, not merely mechanical: tests/test_internal_catalogue_reader.py:200-230 replaced the three source='packaged' capability tests with frame-equality plus exact-provenance plus empty-issues assertions; tests/test_internal_registry.py:929-951 re-pins both _ProviderHandle.__getattr__ branches through _registry.get with the exact "Provider 'pl_imgw' has no attribute 'cache_status'" message; tests/test_map_stations.py:66-88 re-pins the folium optional-dependency contract on rr.map(selection) including the no-IssuePolicyError-in-chain assertion. No assertion was observed weakened to a smoke check, and no suppression was added.

tests/test_discovery.py's surviving products() regressions (exact global vocabulary, per-provider subsets, type(products()) is list, UnknownProviderError on an unknown id) and tests/test_map_stations.py::test_map_survives_map_stations_removal_with_only_required_selection are the explicit survival pins for the two things this step had to keep. Both are present and assert exact values.
summary:
Reviewed PR #142 (base 9725f16, head d157e9a) against the approved m9-s1 plan. Exactly one commit above the base, message 'refactor!: retire the legacy catalogue surface', no attribution footer, no version change (verified __version__ == 0.1.49), no tag, pr-body.md untracked (git ls-files pr-body.md returns nothing) and its content matches section 5 and the posted PR body verbatim. Worktree is tracked-clean; only ?? pr-body.md and ?? pytest-of-nicolaslazaro/ remain.

Headline vision criterion measured, not assumed: `uv run python -c "import rivretrieve; print([n for n in dir(rivretrieve) if not n.startswith('_')])"` prints exactly ['RawMode','as_frame','fetch','fetch_by_provider','find','from_frame','map','pick','products','providers','to_utc'], and hasattr is False for all eight of ProviderHandle, CatalogSource, map_stations, observations, product_info, provider, provider_info, stations.

The four must-still-be-true items were confirmed rather than assumed. (1) products(provider=None) survives with its sorted/deduplicated canonical list and its exact UnknownProviderError, and map(selection) survives with the single required argument — both still have explicit passing regressions. (2) USGS live machinery is untouched: usgs_nwis/module.py keeps observation_source='live', generate_catalogue.py and tests/test_usgs_nwis_generate_catalogue.py are absent from the diff stat, and the live_* provider-info fields remain in the schema and committed rows with no public reader. (3) RawMode publicness is unchanged and no raw=/on_issue= parameter moved on fetch or fetch_by_provider. (4) The four pre-PR repairs are coherent: the three orphaned station_map helpers are gone, _load_folium's missing-dependency contract and _ProviderHandle.__getattr__'s two branches (including the provider-specific message) are re-pinned in tests.

Acceptance scan: `git grep -n -E 'ProviderHandle|CatalogSource|def provider\(|def observations\(|def provider_info\(|def stations\(|def product_info\(|def map_stations\(' d157e9a -- src tests` yields no CatalogSource and no withdrawn top-level definitions; the surviving `def stations(` hits are only the packaged-only provider-module/protocol/registry methods, and the surviving ProviderHandle hits are the private _ProviderHandle plus the test_package absence tuple. No active source= catalogue argument or branch remains anywhere in src or tests.

Gates: `uv run ruff check src tests` reports 'All checks passed!' (no dead imports left behind by the deletion). One detached full-suite run: `uv run pytest -q` -> 1573 passed, 2 skipped in 392s, exit 0, with both skips being the pre-existing pytest.importorskip('folium') tests at tests/test_map_stations.py:161 and :173. That matches the stated figure exactly. Coverage, uv build, ruff format and ruff check --fix were not run, and nothing was edited.

The only quality gaps found are documentation-side and explicitly out of this step's authorised scope (README quickstart and the known station_map docstring); neither should stop the merge. Recommend landing.
